Harden restart-safety per PRD-142 W4-S9: the batched drain must not lose queued signals on clean shutdown (flush-on-stop) and must tolerate process restart (queue is in-process; document the bounded-loss window honestly in the module docstring — no fake durability claims). The PRD-141 US-019 contract holds: no per-call sessions, one session per flush.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — config.py TOOL_SIGNAL_RECORDER_ENABLED default 'false'->'true' with a §6.1-locked docstring (default ON; rollback = one env var; honest bounded-loss note). test_recorder_enabled_by_default asserts config.TOOL_SIGNAL_RECORDER_ENABLED is True AND _enabled()==True. No existing test assumed OFF (the two flag-referencing tests in test_graph_router_negative set it explicitly); acceptance grep sees the '"true"' default.

DONE — test_stop_flushes_queued_signals_no_loss: 3 queued signals all flush exactly once on stop() (no loss, no double-write), queue empties, drain task cleared. test_stop_flushes_in_flight_batch_even_if_drain_blocked: the sentinel wakes a drain blocked mid-collect so its in-flight 'first' still flushes. Spec-compliant, but it makes ALL global (workspace_id IS NULL) used_after edges unreadable — for a tenant read (only exact-ws + meta_sibling) AND for the workspace_id=None system read (only meta_sibling). seed_graph(workspace_id=None) delegates to edge_builder.build_edges(workspace_id=None) (seed_tool_routing_graph.py:65-83), and the passing test_seed_backfills_edges_from_logs shows build_edges(workspace_id=X) stamps the edge workspace_id=X — so a default human-applied seed run with NO --workspace-id produces GLOBAL used_after edges that NO tenant can read post-US-004. Two pre-existing PRD-143 tests exercising global used_after routing now fail on the required CI job (base green). This is not merely stale tests: it is an unreconciled seed/nightly-vs-read gap that can silently make the learned+seeded used_after graph write-only.
userStories.evidence: FAILED on required orchestrator-tests: tests/test_prd143_graph_seed.py::test_seeded_graph_routes_common_intent (L451-458 — _run_seed() with NO workspace_id, then reads WS_A; get_agent expansion missing); ::test_real_used_after_outranks_meta (L604-610 — global used_after excluded, real_chain missing). Source: orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/graph_router.py:498-501; orchestrator/scripts/seed_tool_routing_graph.py:65-83; orchestrator/core/services/edge_builder.py build_edges.
acceptanceCriteria: The required orchestrator-tests CI job is GREEN for HEAD.

Document whether edge_builder.build_edges / seed_graph writes GLOBAL (workspace_id=None) used_after edges when run without a workspace_id, and whether the nightly recompute keys edges by each log's workspace_id or globally.
Prove seeded/nightly used_after edges are still READABLE after US-004 via a positive read test through the REAL _query_edges — no write-only used_after path may remain.

Reconcile: either the seed/nightly writes per-tenant used_after edges (so they survive the meta_sibling-only NULL admission), or the two graph_seed tests are moved to tenant-scoped scenarios AND the global-used_after loss is explicitly signed off.

DECISION (Gerard, §12): if the intended human-applied seed run produces global used_after edges, BLOCK — Gerard decides seed-per-tenant vs accepting the loss of global used_after cold-start (US-007 routing depends on it). Do not silently rewrite the tests to hide the gap.
userStories.notes: US-004 note claims passes:true; the required job is RED on these two tests. meta_sibling globals still cross tenants correctly; only used_after globals are affected. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-29 (Ralph iteration, fresh grep): block STILL LIVE. (1) graph_router.py:495-505 admits workspace_id IS NULL rows ONLY for meta_sibling (meta_global = and_(workspace_id.is_(None), edge_type=='meta_sibling')); tenant read = or_(ws==X, meta_global); None read = meta_global only — no global used_after read path anywhere. (2) seed_tool_routing_graph.py:65-82 seed_graph(workspace_id=None) → edge_builder.build_edges(workspace_id=None); main() passes args.workspace_id which DEFAULTS to None → a default `--yes` seed with no --workspace-id writes GLOBAL used_after edges no read path can surface. (3) tests/test_prd143_graph_seed.py::{test_seeded_graph_routes_common_intent,test_real_used_after_outranks_meta} still FAIL (2 failed / 10 passed; AssertionError, fixture-based — no DB). §12 DECISION for Gerard, two real options: (A) seed/nightly writes PER-TENANT used_after (key each edge by its log's workspace_id; operator seeds per --workspace-id) — preserves used_after cold-start, changes runbook + build_edges aggregation semantics; or (B) ACCEPT loss of global used_after cold-start (used_after only from organic per-tenant learning; US-007 seeded CLUSTERS still cold-start via affinities/centroids, which do NOT read used_after edges) and move the two tests to tenant-scoped scenarios with the loss signed off. Builder RALPH_BLOCKED here — must NOT silently rewrite the tests (AC #5). All US stories DONE; RVW-1/3/4 are code-complete + locally green — their shared 'orchestrator-tests GREEN for HEAD' gate cascades off this single decision. RVW-5 done: acceptance now honestly RED on this.

userStories.title: US-010 cluster hot-actions bypass admin-tier gating (fail-closed violation, latent until the flip)
userStories.description: GraphRouter._merge_cluster_hot_actions (graph_router.py:428-446) appends a matched cluster's action_names_hot into entry_nodes with NO admin/super_admin re-check — unlike organic entry nodes which are role-filtered by rank_actions(exclude_admin, include_super_admin) at graph_router.py:191-198. The only downstream net, _drop_super_admin_chains (graph_router.py:714-731, called at :221-222), filters super_admin_only ONLY — never admin_only. The US-007 seed _load_action_categories (seed_tool_routing_graph.py:126-139) excludes su but NOT admin, and organic clusters are built from cross-tenant aggregate logs, so action_names_hot can legitimately contain admin_only actions. Net: rank_chains(exclude_admin=True) can return an admin_only action to a caller that explicitly excluded admin — violating US-014 AC 'tier gating (super_admin_only, admin) unchanged and fail-closed' (PRD-232 §110). Currently masked because both live consumers re-gate downstream (PlatformActionsSection re-filters exclude_admin=True; smart_tool_router only narrows an already role-gated available_tools) and TOOL_ROUTING_GRAPH is default OFF — but it is a latent fail-open that activates exactly when the flag flips (this PRD's goal) or when any future caller trusts rank_chains' exclude_admin contract.
userStories.evidence: orchestrator/modules/tools/discovery/graph_router.py:428-446 (_merge_cluster_hot_actions, no role filter), :281 (call site), :714-731 (_drop_super_admin_chains drops super_admin_only only), :221-222; orchestrator/scripts/seed_tool_routing_graph.py:126-139 (admin_only not excluded from seeded clusters).
acceptanceCriteria: DONE (option b, generalized exit net) — _drop_super_admin_chains → _drop_ineligible_chains(chains, exclude_admin, include_super_admin), now called UNCONDITIONALLY in rank_chains (was gated on `not include_super_admin`). It drops super_admin_only chains unless include_super_admin=True AND admin_only chains when exclude_admin=True, over the WHOLE expanded surface — so cluster action_names_hot (US-010) AND edge-expansion targets both get re-gated, not just entry nodes. Same registry role check as organic ranking; su behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.

DONE — tests/test_prd232_us010_cluster_aware_reads.py::test_cluster_hot_admin_action_dropped_for_operator_but_kept_for_admin: a matched cluster whose action_names_hot carries an admin_only + an su + an operator action → rank_chains(exclude_admin=True) surfaces ONLY the operator action (admin AND su dropped); rank_chains(exclude_admin=False) surfaces the admin action but STILL drops su (proves exclude_admin gates it, not a blanket drop). _rank helper gained exclude_admin/include_super_admin passthrough (backward-compatible defaults).

PENDING (shared CI gate) — RVW-4 adds fail-closed coverage with no current CI failure; local CI-faithful-order run 121 passed (eval_graph_mode→graph_router→graph_negative→selection_at_scale→su_surface→prd177 tenant/chain-hints→us010→us014). orchestrator-tests goes GREEN once the P232-RVW-2 Test-2 §12 block clears. NOTE: test_su_present is order-fragile ONLY in the direct eval_graph_mode→su_surface pairing (US-014-introduced narrowing dependency); CI's alphabetical order runs test_prd143_boundary_sweep + test_prd143_selection_at_scale (both DB-free, both sort before su_surface) between them, re-establishing clean module state → CI-safe.
userStories.notes: Code-review HIGH #1 fixed via a single fail-closed exit net (reviewer's option b) — the graph layer is now fail-closed on admin AND su on its own, ahead of the TOOL_ROUTING_GRAPH flip. _drop_super_admin_chains had no direct callers (only a comment mention, updated). passes stays FALSE only on the shared CI-green gate (P232-RVW-2 §12 block). Local: 121 passed CI-faithful order; 26 passed us010+graph_negative+su_graph.

userStories.title: acceptance-prd232.sh is structurally false-green — its test net cannot see unchanged-file regressions
userStories.description: The acceptance script backend-test step (scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd232.sh:26-35) runs ONLY the changed test files (CHT = git diff --name-only ...tests/*.py). All 8 required-CI regressions in P232-RVW-1..3 live in UNCHANGED test files (test_prd143_su_surface, test_prd143_selection_at_scale, test_prd143_graph_seed, test_prd225_asks_model), so the script exits 0 while the required orchestrator-tests job is RED. This is the exact 'locally-SKIPPING -> false-green while required CI is RED' trap; it let US-004/US-007/US-014 be marked passes:true against red CI.
userStories.evidence: scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd232.sh:26-35 (CHT scope); branch run 33264107121 orchestrator-tests=failure vs base run 33230270680=success.
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — acceptance-prd232.sh gained an explicit RVW-5 block (option b, network-free) that runs the four regression-prone suites (test_prd143_su_surface, test_prd143_selection_at_scale, test_prd143_graph_seed, test_prd225_asks_model) AFTER the diff-scoped net; any failure sets FAIL=1. Empirically confirmed the trap: 3 of the 4 (su_surface/selection_at_scale/prd225_asks_model — the files RVW-1/RVW-3 modified) ARE in the changed-test net, but test_prd143_graph_seed is NOT (RVW-2 unfixed → file untouched → diff-net structurally blind to it). The explicit block is what surfaces it.

DONE — verified: combined four-suite run = 2 failed / 55 passed (only graph_seed's 2 RVW-2 tests red) → pytest exit 1 → the new block sets FAIL=1 → acceptance-prd232.sh exits 1. A local acceptance PASS now requires all four contract suites green, i.e. the required-CI reds (RVW-1..3) all cleared; it can no longer coexist with a RED required orchestrator-tests job for the same HEAD. Right now acceptance CORRECTLY reports RED because RVW-2 (§12 Gerard block) is still open.
